channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: How Many Fine-Tuning Examples Do You Actually Need
item.description: Fine-tuning does not need thousands of examples to work. It needs the right examples, tested the right way.

item.title: Fine-Tuning Synonyms: Why Precise Language Matters
item.description: Calling everything 'fine-tuning' hides what you actually did. Precise method language is a reproducibility issue, not pedantry.

item.title: Why LLM Wikis and Glossaries Disagree on Basic Terms
item.description: Why does every LLM glossary define 'hallucination' or 'grounding' differently? A practical guide to choosing and defending your own working definitions.

item.title: Data Science Versus Data Analytics: Why It Matters
item.description: Same buzzwords, different jobs. Here is the concrete distinction between data science and data analytics, and why conflating them causes bad hires and worse projects.

item.title: Model Evaluation Versus Threat Research: What Gets Tested
item.description: Benchmarks measure capability on fixed tasks; threat research probes what a model could do in the hands of a determined, resourceful actor. They are not interchangeable.

item.title: What Counts as a Large Language Model, Really
item.description: Large language model has become a marketing word as much as a technical one. Here is what the definition should hinge on, and why the wiki version only gets you halfway.

item.title: Computer Vision in Five Years: What Still Matters
item.description: Models and architectures will churn, but data discipline, evaluation rigour, and error analysis will still matter in five years. Here is what to actually invest in.

item.title: Machine Learning Syllabi Compared: What Maps to a Job
item.description: Most ML courses teach models first and evaluation last. Real jobs run the other way round. Here is where the gap bites.

item.title: What an Internship Teaches That a Course Cannot
item.description: Courses optimise for clean data and clean metrics. Internships force you to confront messy data, moving targets, and stakeholders, which is where real skill is built.

item.title: Prompt Engineering Certificate or Portfolio: What Gets Checked
item.description: A certificate proves you sat through a course. A portfolio proves you can ship. Here is what hiring managers actually look at first.

item.title: Computer Vision From Pixels to Predictions, One Example
item.description: How a handful of pixel values turns into a confident prediction, traced step by step through one small worked example.

item.title: The ML Algorithms You Should Understand Before Any Library
item.description: Before you import scikit-learn or PyTorch, understand linear models, trees, and gradient descent by hand. It changes how you debug.

item.title: Data Science Degree Versus Minor: What Each Prepares You For
item.description: A degree builds the judgement to design a pipeline from scratch; a minor builds the fluency to use one well. Neither is a shortcut to the other.

item.title: Prompt Engineering Guide: Structuring One Prompt from Scratch
item.description: A practical walkthrough of building one prompt from a vague task to a reliable, testable instruction set.

item.title: How to Evaluate a Machine Learning Definition Before Trusting It
item.description: A practical checklist for interrogating machine learning definitions before you let them shape your assumptions, your splits, or your conclusions.

item.title: Computer Vision Jobs Decoded: What 'Entry Level' Really Means
item.description: 'Entry level' in computer vision postings rarely means beginner. Here is how to decode the requirements and apply with confidence.

item.title: ML Engineer Salary Bands Explained Through the Work
item.description: Forget the title. Salary bands in machine learning track the judgement required by the work, not years of experience or a label on a contract.

item.title: What a Prompt Engineering Course Should Teach but Skips
item.description: Clever phrasing is easy to teach. Rigorous evaluation of prompts, under variance and leakage, is the part courses usually skip.

item.title: Prompt Engineering Salary Claims: What the Job Actually Pays For
item.description: The eye-catching prompt engineer salary figures are really paying for evaluation, debugging and systems judgement, not magic phrasing.

item.title: Common ML Algorithms Grouped by the Problem They Solve
item.description: A practical map of machine learning methods organised by the underlying problem they solve, not by buzzword or library.
